title: Token SLI Reconciler Daemon and Anomaly Ingestor
creator: Priya Kapoor
description: Build a reconciler service (Token SLI Reconciler Daemon) that merges token-level latency SLIs from multiple upstream collectors (edge eBPF traces, admission/kv telemetry, and synthetic prober) into a single canonical SLI stream per tenant+route. The reconciler will compute reconciled quantiles, emit delta/anomaly events when sources diverge beyond configured thresholds, and forward reconciled SLI time-series to the central metrics store and a lightweight anomaly ingest topic. This enables downstream dashboards, automated circuit-breaker tuning, and region-failover triggers to consume a single authoritative SLI with provenance attached.
acceptance_criteria: Daemon reads from three sources concurrently: eBPF token timing stream, admission telemetry (admit/evict/kvs), and synthetic SLI prober. Failure of any single upstream must not stop reconciliation.
For each tenant+route+sequence_bucket, reconciler emits a reconciled p50/p95/p99 time-series and a "delta" event when two sources disagree by >15% for p95 or >20ms for p99.
Reconciled time-series written to metrics cluster within 5s of ingest and labeled with source_provenance and reconciliation_score.
Anomaly events published to anomaly-ingest Kafka topic with tenant, route, region, window_start, window_end, diff_metrics, and suggested-action tags.
Dashboards updated to consume reconciled series and show side-by-side source comparisons with provenance toggles.
Integration tests simulate source divergence and validate delta events and downstream circuit-breaker binding (mocked).
design_notes: Use a stateless daemon that maintains a sliding window (60s by default) per key; store checkpoints in Redis for leader failover.
Reconciliation algorithm: weighted median where weights are based on source_confidence (synthetic=0.6, eBPF=0.3, admission=0.1) with tunable weighting via config store.
Provenance: include top-2 contributing sources and per-metric confidence score so runbooks can explain anomalies.
Backpressure: if metrics cluster is slow, buffer reconciled points to S3-backed queue and degrade to event-only mode (emit anomalies, skip timeseries) to preserve alerts.
Security: metrics contain no raw request payloads; only aggregated token-latency histograms and counts. Ensure KMS encryption on checkpoint store.
implementation_steps: 1) Prototype reconciliation library in Python with ingest adapters for eBPF JSONL, admission protobuf, and synthetic prober CSV.
2) Implement reconciler daemon (Go service) exposing Prometheus health/metrics and config via Feature Flags.
3) Add Redis checkpointing and leader-election using Redlock.
4) Publish reconciled series to metrics cluster (Grafana Tempo-compatible labels) and anomaly events to Kafka topic anomaly-ingest.
5) Create integration harness that can replay historical traces to validate reconciliation stability over long windows.
6) Wire up dashboard panels and add a reconciled-to-source diff visualization in Console: expose toggle for provenance and threshold controls.
7) Hook anomaly events to circuit-breaker control plane for evaluation in canary (no auto-action for initial rollout).
test_plan: Unit tests for reconciliation math with randomized weighted inputs and edge cases (missing source, zero-count windows).
Integration tests that spin up eBPF-simulator, admission-harness, and synth-prober to validate end-to-end latency from source to metrics cluster (<5s).
Chaos test: kill leader reconciler during high traffic and verify follower picks up checkpoints and resumes with <15s lag.
Load test: ensure reconciler can sustain 1k tenant+route keys per instance with 60s window on our staging Redis/metrics topology.
Alerting verification: anomalies produce alerts to the SRE Slack channel and create PagerDuty incidents when thresholds exceed high-impact rules.
rollout_plan: Alpha: run reconciler for a small set of internal tenants in passive mode (emit anomalies but do not feed circuit-breaker).
Beta: enable writing reconciled timeseries for beta tenants and add dashboard panels; collect feedback from platform and SRE.
Canary: enable anomaly hooks for automated suggestions to circuit-breaker tuning for 10% of production routes (monitor closely).
GA: enable reconciler for all tenants, feed reconciled SLI to dashboards, and allow opt-in for auto-suggested circuit-breaker parameter updates.
Fallback: switch reconciler to event-only mode on metrics cluster degradation; documented in runbook.
